title: census.py check retries a name-resolution or connection error once and counts it apart from a blocked host
goal: census.py check retries a source whose fetch fails with a name-resolution or connection error (the 2026-09-26 log has 10 rows with 'nodename nor servname provided') once after a short pause, in the same run; a source still failing gets note dns or connect, which census.py summary counts apart from blocked and from HTTP errors, naming the hosts, so a transient resolver failure is retried by a tool, not handed to a reader; a host denied by policy keeps note blocked.

gates.question: How long is the pause before census.py check retries a fetch that failed with a name-resolution or connection error (the pause sits outside the per-host semaphore, one worker thread waits)?
Which fetch errors count as a connection error (note connect) that census.py check retries once?
options: refused, reset, unreachable and timed out
refused, reset and unreachable only; a timeout stays a plain error
gates.recommendation: refused, reset, unreachable and timed out
gates.answer: refused, reset, unreachable and timed out

gates.question: Do rows noted dns or connect stay in the phase-2 reading queue (as blocked rows do not)?
options: stay in the queue: a reader can fetch them another way, as the 2026-09-26 readers did with curl --resolve
leave the queue like blocked rows
gates.recommendation: stay in the queue: a reader can fetch them another way, as the 2026-09-26 readers did with curl --resolve
gates.answer: stay in the queue: a reader can fetch them another way, as the 2026-09-26 readers did with curl --resolve

notes: Premise from kb/public/_census/2026-09-26.csv (tally run 2026-10-10): 10 live rows with evidence 'HTTP error: [Errno 8] nodename nor servname provided' went to phase 2 (7 updated, 3 confirmed), so a reader fetched pages the check could not. A host that still fails after the retry stays a counted dns row; the tool does not change resolvers.
